scope: Local repair verification for three hosted failures and a diagnostic comparison for the shared-cook runtime warning. Hosted Xcode 26.3 and local Xcode 27.1.

recipe.checks: Exact original source URL, notes, three servings and six wraps persisted; four servings and eight wraps after the weekly edit. One meal and its grocery proposal were read before applying.
recipe.localResult: 4 passed, zero warnings. A controlled accessibility delay reproduced an expired value check with the exact URL present before and after.

renderedSearch.checks: The exact post-restart search field value and matching row or empty result share the existing eight-second result deadline. The timed 20 searches and 20 checkoffs remain separate from this interaction.
renderedSearch.localResult: 1 passed, zero warnings. The local Release run retained 500 rows and all 20 checked identities. The original test also passed on a fresh local fixture. Hosted timing thresholds still require the hosted environment.

keyboard.checks: Five fresh editors each received one tap. Each positive run kept the amount at 3 and dismissed both Done and the keyboard. Each observed target was 44 × 44 points. One deliberate tap inside the field kept the keyboard and Done visible and failed the center check.
keyboard.localResult: 3 stock-review tests passed, zero warnings. The extra minimum-size assertions passed the five-point test in a separate run.

sharedCookReadback.hosted: Five functional cases passed. The strict checker failed on a runtime issue during the edited cook readback, 0.566 seconds after Play completed. The issue lacked the description attachment and symbolized frames. Session and process logs did not recover the blocking stack.
sharedCookReadback.local: A replay on iPhone 17, iOS 26.2 reproduced a warning between Play and Pause. A standalone speech control reached natural completion and reproduced the same 20 framework frames. Audio-session activation alone and voice lookup alone did not reproduce the issue.
sharedCookReadback.status: Hosted stack attribution remains open. The runtime warning still fails the gate.
